sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: perception versus reaction time, following-distance numbers, glare direction, headwind versus tailwind, dust storm steps and rain timing
Look-alike numbers and responses from the braking, weather and dust storm pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec16-R01 | anchor: A01
Perception time and reaction time each average 0.75 seconds, and together they make the 1.5 seconds an average driver needs before braking begins. [A01]
Why it matters: group stopping time; difficulty three; confusable sec16-F03 versus sec16-F04; prereq sec16-F05.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec16-R02 | anchor: A01
The everyday minimum is a 3-second following distance, while slippery roads call for doubling it to 6 seconds or more. [A01]
Why it matters: group following distance; difficulty two; confusable sec16-F08 versus sec16-F10.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec16-R03 | anchor: A01
When someone behind you wants to pass, the right move is to slow down, not to speed up. [A01]
Why it matters: group being passed; difficulty two; prereq sec16-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec16-R04 | anchor: A02
With the sun ahead of you, you face the glare, but with the sun behind you, oncoming drivers face it and may not see you. [A02]
Why it matters: group sun glare; difficulty two; confusable sec16-F19 versus sec16-F21.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec16-R05 | anchor: A02
Crosswinds are most likely when you come out of a sheltered stretch into open space, and they can push you toward the edge or the middle of the road. [A02]
Why it matters: group wind; difficulty two; prereq sec16-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec16-R06 | anchor: A03
A headwind calls for more acceleration and firmer steering, while a tailwind calls for slowing and braking earlier. [A03]
Why it matters: group wind; difficulty two; confusable sec16-F30 versus sec16-F31.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec16-R07 | anchor: A03
In a severe dust storm you leave the highway completely, avoiding both the travel lane and the emergency lane, and then switch off your lights and release the brake. [A03]
Why it matters: group dust storms; difficulty three; confusable sec16-F36 versus sec16-F37.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec16-R08 | anchor: A03
Pull off early in a dust storm, before visibility drops, rather than waiting until you can no longer see to leave the road safely. [A03]
Why it matters: group dust storms; difficulty two; prereq sec16-F34.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec16-R09 | anchor: A03
Rain calls for a gap of at least 6 seconds, while the 30 minutes figure marks the especially slippery period after rain starts. [A03]
Why it matters: group rain numbers; difficulty three; confusable sec16-F42 versus sec16-F43.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec16-R10 | anchor: A03
In heavy rain, tires can lose all road contact at 50 mph, while worn, bald or under-inflated tires can lose it at much lower speeds. [A03]
Why it matters: group hydroplaning; difficulty three; confusable sec16-F44 versus sec16-F45.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec16-R11 | anchor: A03
When towing a trailer as a truck or bus passes on the left, you first move right and slow down, and then speed up only gently as it passes. [A03]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty three; prereq sec16-F29.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0055]
